name: Linear actuators
summary: Motors with a screw drive that push and pull in a straight line: recliners, beds, desks and lifts.
uses: Lifting and tilting heavy things slowly
identify: A motor on the side of a long tube with a rod that slides out, often 24–29V DC, under power recliners, adjustable and hospital beds, in standing desks, TV lifts and treadmill incline drives. Many push several thousand newtons, enough to crush fingers.
test: Feed it 12–24V DC and it should extend; swap the wires and it retracts. Built-in limit switches stop it at each end.
